newsitem.title: USA: Fifth victim of Miami plane crash identified.
newsitem.headline: Fifth victim of Miami plane crash identified.

text.p: Investigators have identified a fifth victim from the crash of a cargo plane on take-off from Miami airport, the only person known to have been killed on the ground, police said Sunday.
The badly charred body of Renato Alvarez was identified from medical records. He leaves a wife and a 20-month-old son.
Alvarez had been driving home with lunch for his family at the time of Thursday's crash, his wife Maria said when she first reported he was missing.
"It's really sad, a tragedy," police spokeswoman Nelda Fonticiella said.

Investigator Robert Benzon said the car was "scraped off the roadway" by the Fine Air DC-8 when the plane plummeted from the sky, ploughed across a main road and disintegrated in flames in a busy warehouse district.
The four other victims discovered so far were the plane's pilot, co-pilot, flight engineer and a security guard. Officials have said it was a miracle more people on the ground were not killed.
The plane was bound for Santo Domingo, Dominican Republic, carrying a load of denim for clothes factories.
Benzon, of the National Transportation Safety Board, said overloading did not cause the crash. Bad weather has also been eliminated.

"There's a lot of things on the table," he told reporters Saturday. "A shift in cargo is still in there. A malfunction is still there. We don't really have leading theories. There are several. We always look at pilot error."
He said radar records showed the plane had climbed to 600 feet (200 metres) before it dropped from the sky -- high enough to indicate overloading was not the problem.
The Miami Herald had quoted former Fine Air employees as saying the company frequently overloaded its planes.
